video_title: The Deadline For Jalen Duren's Extension Is Days Away | Chris Mannix & Evan Turner

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons are handling Jalen Duren's contract situation the right way
quotes.excerpt: I think the Pistons are handling the correct way to be completely honest with you.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: What do you make of all this? And what do you think the Pistons should do right now about Jalen Duren?

text_blocks.speaker: Evan Turner
text_blocks.text: I think the Pistons are handling the correct way to be completely honest with you. I think they're rewarding him for a high level. I think they're trying to think for the future. They're going to give him $40 million a year to play basketball. They're trying to build a great team around you, but most importantly, a top 10 player like Cade Cunningham.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Duren is best suited as a third option on a championship team
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Duren, if it came down to like a championship team or whatever, he's a third option.
quotes.quote: Jalen Duren, if it came down to like a championship team or whatever, he's a third option. He would be best as a third option on that team because no matter what, you need reliable scoring and a strong backcourt or a wing in order to make it in this league and to be even more dominant. They already lost Tobias Harris, he's going up the street, that was 18 points per game. I feel as though Detroit's handling it the right way.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons would have maxed Jalen Duren if he hadn't struggled in the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: If Jalen Duren had pulled his hamstring on the final day of the regular season, we wouldn't be having this conversation.
quotes.quote: The facts are that if Jalen Duren had pulled his hamstring on the final day of the regular season, we wouldn't be having this conversation because the Pistons would have maxed him out. What is giving the Pistons reason for pause is what happened in the playoffs, which were that disaster for Jalen Duren. His numbers were basically cut in half, he was outplayed by other bigs, and he just didn't look like the franchise center that he looked like for most of the regular season.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons are in a difficult spot regarding Jalen Duren's contract
quotes.excerpt: The Pistons are kind of between a rock and a hard place too here.
quotes.quote: The Pistons are kind of between a rock and a hard place too here because they can't just lose him for nothing. They trade away Isaiah Stewart, he was a part of the fabric of that new old-school Detroit basketball. He was the Rick Mahorn of this era. They lose Tobias Harris, a productive guy for the two years. The Pistons last two years have engineered one of the great revivals in the NBA. You're replacing him with John Collins, who's younger, I guess, but John Collins has been moved around a lot.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons face significant risk if Jalen Duren signs the qualifying offer
quotes.excerpt: If he signs that qualifying offer, the Pistons are in a world of trouble.
quotes.quote: You need Jalen Duren. You got to get him back. You're not going to lose him this year because the worst thing that can happen is he signs the qualifying offer. But if he signs that qualifying offer, the Pistons are in a world of trouble because I don't think you can trade a guy after he signs the qualifying offer. If that's the case, you lose Jalen Duren for little or nothing. They need him there, or they need like Domantas Sabonis to replace him, or Miles Turner maybe to replace him. They need an actual asset in there to replace him.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The financial risk of signing a qualifying offer for Jalen Duren
quotes.excerpt: You sign the qualifying offer, that's money you're never going to get back.
quotes.quote: The qualifying offer is different because in a lot of contracts, like let's use Jalen Brunson as an example, Jalen Brunson took less money from the Knicks. Well, Jalen Brunson can make that up. You sign the qualifying offer, that's money you're never going to get back. You're never going to be able to recoup the difference between the one year $10 million qualifying offer that you signed and the $50 million average salary that you would sign if you're Jalen Duren there. So it's a lot of money and it's a big bet on yourself. Remember when Kristaps Porzingis was leaving the Knicks and he was threatening to sign the qualifying offer when he got to Dallas? He didn't do that, because guys don't do that.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Confusion over reports of a weight clause in Jalen Duren's contract
quotes.excerpt: Why are we even talking about a weight clause with Jalen Duren?
quotes.quote: What do you make also of the reports that the Pistons want to include a weight clause in this contract? Trajan Langdon, the GM there came from New Orleans. There was a weight clause in Zion Williamson's contract for good reason. Whatever you want to say about Jalen Duren, he looks like he's carved out of a rock. Why are we even talking about a weight clause with Jalen Duren? Nobody in the NBA can really explain this to me.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Mobley is a better player than Jalen Duren
quotes.excerpt: Who's better, Evan Mobley or Jalen Duren?
quotes.quote: Do you think who's better, Evan Mobley or Jalen Duren? Evan Mobley. He's a former defensive player of the year and while we are not in love with all of the offensive things that Evan Mobley does, he's still a developing offensive player.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner is grateful for Evan Mobley's contributions
quotes.excerpt: I'm grateful of what Evan Mobley brings to the game.
quotes.quote: I'm grateful of what Evan Mobley brings to the game and I can confidently say like I don't expect whatever we're waiting for to show up. And I can say the same thing with Jalen Duren. Where they're at, I think they peaked. Besides like maybe playing well playoff wise, but even when you sit there and like he's a ball handler, he's making assists, like man, some strong ass passes. I don't want to see that shit. We're in trouble if Jalen Duren is handling the ball.

quotes.speaker: Evan Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evan Turner suggests the Pistons should target Domantas Sabonis
quotes.excerpt: I would try to go get Domantas Sabonis.
quotes.quote: I would try to go get Domantas Sabonis. I would go get a real bruiser who's going to hit you in your face, not going to get punked by you know the 15th best center in the playoff times and he can drop dimes and literally if you took away the Sacramento Kings and the NBA vibe, he'd be an MVP candidate every year for how he plays and all around and just even being thorough in that Kings system. He shows up night in and night out.
